summary: Read the complete supplied markdown, including supplementary analyses and references, and checked every cited PDF page for the five requested estimates. All 40 source quotations match the PDF after whitespace normalization. The recorded means, SDs, regression coefficients, SEs, tests, degrees of freedom, p-values, and reported d belong to the stated outcomes and arms. The negative AI-rate t statistic is printed as recorded and must not be sign-corrected. The high-quality fluency outcome counts ideas meeting both originality and usefulness thresholds, so construct fluency and higher_is more_ideas are correct. The three main contrasts use the reported final sample of 96 people, each completing every condition (PDF pp. 7-8); these are repeated people counts, not independent observation counts. Their participant se_basis follows the stated Subject ID random effect (PDF p. 15), with the unresolved team dependence already documented. Both perspective-taking quality rates score adopted task-output ideas and are eligible standalone contrasts, notwithstanding their later use in mediation. Their analysis-specific counts, rate aggregation, and SD levels are not established, so the null fields are appropriate. The human-rate analysis is repeated-measures ANOVA; the AI-rate analysis explicitly uses independent-samples t-tests, supporting the recorded paired and null within_person values respectively, with the repeated-design inconsistency documented. The other requested coding fields are supported. Both mechanical se_basis warnings are false positives against the supplied rules: creativity-codebook.md section 10 explicitly permits unclear for a printed test whose analysis unit is not established, and extraction-spec.md includes and defines that value. Keep unclear for both rates; not_reported would incorrectly imply that no uncertainty was printed. The completeness check found no missing eligible outcome or contrast: the extraction contains all three contrasts for usefulness, originality, ordinary fluency, and high-quality fluency, plus both reported quality-rate contrasts. Process measures, baseline self-reports, and mediator-adjusted or indirect effects are appropriately excluded; figure-only mediation totals do not require numerical extraction under rule 1.
